transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Camilo Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Erica Voss (Halcyon VP Eng); Mike Tran (Halcyon SRE); Sofia Lee (Halcyon Product); Aaron Brooks (Halcyon Security)

Auto-summary: Customer still cold on reliability after last week's latency spike; team converged on cache-dominant root cause but need concrete perf runs and security artifacts to re-enable pilot expansion. Next steps and owners captured.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-transcript with occasional errors) ---
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and this is Priya our SE, Camilo will help coordinate next steps, we wanted to run through what we learned and propose a mitigation path.
[00:14] Erica: Thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We had an all-hands after the incident, execs want confidence that this is not going to recur when traffic scales. So, what do you have for us?
[00:27] Priya: Yeah hi, super quick recap - our working hypothesis is that the latency burst was driven by a coordinated pattern: cache evictions in the prefix/KV cache layer combined with back-to-back cold starts on the dedicated GPU pool, leading to token regen and tail latency spikes. There's also a small probability that a mis-sized batcher window exacerbated queuing.
[00:48] Mike: When you say kv-cache eviction, is that the customer side cache or Redwood's internal prefix cache? We're seeing a lot of confusion internally about where state is..
[01:00] Priya: Good question — it's Redwood's runtime prefix cache (the K V cache in the serving runtime). The trace you sent shows a pattern where many unique prefixes were requested after a deployment, causing the cache to thrash. On top of that, the GPU workers scaled up but did cold-model loads which increased p99.
[01:20] Sofia: Quick clarifying, is this more likely on hosted or dedicated? Our security team prefers dedicated to isolate workloads but they worry about capacity.
[01:34] Jordan: Both modes can see it but it's more visible on dedicated when pools are right-sized for steady load and then hit a burst. Hosted has autoscaling + more spare capacity so it sometimes hides the pattern.
[01:47] Aaron: From security, we need audit logs showing access to model artifacts, and a KMS flow diagram. Also want assurance that cache contents aren't persisted to logs.
[02:01] Priya: Understood. We'll include audit-log samples. The cache is in-memory and not persisted to disk; we can show memory map and eviction metrics but obviously we will sanitize traces.
[02:14] Mike: In the trace there were also frequent re-tries from our edge -- we were trying to be resilient but that probably increased load. Some of those retries lined up with deployment markers.
[02:30] Priya: Yeah retries amplify the effect. In modern LLM serving the tail is sensitive to synchronous replays.
[02:40] Jordan: Here's our mitigation plan (high-level) — short-term: tweak batcher window and add a small warm-start pool to avoid cold loads during deployments; medium-term: prefix-aware cache warming tied to canary traffic; long-term: KV eviction policy improvements and telemetry hooks to surface thrash earlier.
[03:01] Erica: That sounds promising. For the warm-start pool, can we guarantee no data cross-talk? Security will ask.
[03:13] Priya: Yes, warm-start pools use the same isolation as dedicated pool — memory is ephemeral per container, and we can pin model variants per tenant. We'll provide the design doc.
[03:25] Mike: Needed: the exact params you want us to change in our autoscaler and the expected impact.
[03:33] Priya: We'll propose a candidate: reduce max_batch_latency from 50ms to 35ms for your profile and enable a 3-node warm pool for rolling deploys. That should cut p99 under burst by ~25-40% in our internal sims.
[03:50] Jordan: We ran an initial sim on a 12h trace and saw tail reduce but not eliminate. Hence the need for replay with your full 36h trace.
[04:05] Sofia: Are there any feature flags we can toggle without a deploy?
[04:11] Priya: A couple in the control plane: prefix_cache_eviction_threshold and batch_latency_sla override. We can flip them with no model redeploy, just a control-plane change with rollback.
[04:25] Aaron: On compliance — we need retention settings and proof of SOC2 scope. Also, if you change batch windows, will that affect output determinism and auditability?
[04:38] Jordan: It won't change model outputs. Batching affects latency and hardware utilization but not inference results. We'll also provide a short appendix on auditability.
[04:50] [crosstalk] Erica: Okay that's helpful.
[05:00] Priya: I want to call out an oddity in the trace — around 13:12 UTC there was a sudden spike in unique user prompts that aligns with a marketing campaign, which increased entropy of prefixes and reduced cache hit rate. So this is partially behavioral.
[05:18] Mike: Ah yes that was when we launched a new site feature. Good to know.
[05:25] Jordan: So remediation will be a combo: infra tuning + client-side rate limiting/gradual rollout of hot prompts.
[05:35] Sofia: For our execs, we also want a timeline to restore confidence and a gating criteria to resume pilot expansion.
[05:44] Camilo: Proposed gating: successful 4-hour on-site bench with p95/p99 within agreed thresholds, security artifacts delivered and a follow-up review.
[05:55] Erica: That's reasonable. What thresholds are we talking about?
[06:00] Priya: For Halcyon profile, target p95 < 180ms and p99 < 500ms under bursty 95th percentile traffic from your trace. We'll tune the exact thresholds before the bench.
[06:15] Aaron: Please also show audit logs for request IDs and token-level cost breakdowns. That's a compliance ask.
[06:22] Jordan: We'll include token-level cost breakdowns in the appendices.
[06:28] [10:12] Priya: Walkthrough of the replay plan: we'll take your 36h anonymized trace, feed it into our local runtime with the same model and quantization settings, run with and without warm pool and with different batch windows. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, GPU mem high-water, and eviction rate.
[10:45] Mike: Will that require us to open a port or share GCP logs?
[10:51] Priya: We'll accept either a sanitized trace file or a temporary GCS bucket with the trace; no need to expose internal ports.
[11:05] Erica: On the point of evictions, what's the plan to change eviction policy? Is it LRU-based?
[11:12] Priya: Currently approximate LRU tuned for memory and seq length; we propose prioritizing prefixes with high reuse score and pin recently-seen canary prefixes during deploy. It's a small change but requires telemetry additions.
[11:30] Jordan: Also want to be transparent: if the replay shows it's not primarily cache eviction we'll broaden to look at underlying kernel swapping and GPU scheduling. But the trace strongly points to cache thrash.
[11:45] Sofia: Assuming the replay tests pass, how long to roll to production safely?
[11:52] Priya: With canary and warm pool, we can do a staged rollout in 48-72 hours with continuous monitoring and an automatic rollback on SLA breach.
[12:03] Erica: Good. On the security doc, Aaron wants KMS flow for model keys and where logs land.
[12:12] Aaron: Also multi-tenant protections — are model weights shared on hardware between tenants?
[12:18] Priya: No, weights are isolated per container; shared caches are only for prefixes and are logically partitioned. We'll include the partitioning diagram.
[12:29] [20:00] Jordan: Okay to summarize: 1) Redwood runs the 36h replay and shares results, 2) Jordan shares the security appendix, 3) schedule on-site perf bench, 4) Camilo coordinates the gating criteria and exec readout. Any other asks?
[20:18] Erica: Please include a simple changelog of the small control-plane flags and an expected rollback path. Execs like to see the undo.
[20:27] Jordan: Will do.
[20:33] Mike: One more operational ask — can Redwood provide a lightweight Grafana dashboard template for our SREs to monitor eviction rate/avg batch size/hot prefix counts?
[20:44] Priya: Yes, we'll export a dashboard JSON and an example alert rule.
[20:50] Camilo: I'll own calendar ops. We'll tentatively aim for the week of 8/24 for the on-site.
[21:00] Sofia: Sounds good. Also, could you send a short one-pager for execs summarizing root cause and the gating criteria?
[21:09] Jordan: Yep, we'll include that with the security appendix.
[21:15] [wrap-up] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of owners and due dates — Priya replay by 8/19, Jordan security docs by 8/14, Mike provides the trace by 8/16, Camilo books on-site by 8/18. We'll reconvene after the replay.
[21:35] Erica: Thanks, that's helpful — look forward to the replay data.
[21:40] Jordan: Thanks all.

--- End transcript ---
